newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa still weak but room to move higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa still weak but room to move higher.

text.p: MARCH Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Cocoa futures are likely to retain their bearish tone in the short term but upside potential in the market could also gather pace and spark a rally out of a major downtrend channel, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
London's benchmark March contract has created a downtrend channel extending from lows around 990 stg which were last seen in the middle of October.
"Cocoa is still weak but there is a possibility of a move to the upside," said Darren Gurner, a technical analyst at Sucden.
A good close could see the market quickly realise its upside potential and race higher, he said.
"If it moves above 950 we could see it up to 968 and even 975 -- and the momentum of the market suggests that it's going up a bit," he said.
Both March's five and 10-day momentum indicators are rising quite steeply out of negative territory and its slow stochastic K-line has already pushed above the 30-value oversold level.
On the downside, the trendline's extrapolation suggested that support could stretch to as low as 910 stg, with initial support pegged at 930 followed by 925 stg, Gurner said.
"If the channel holds we'll look for the market to move down towards the lower levels around 910."
Traders called the London market to open around two stg lower than Monday's close due to currency movements.
Elsewhere, Ivory Coast set reference rates to be paid to cocoa buyers and exporters on Monday, clearing the way for the 1996/97 season to get fully underway.
Details were not immediately available, but trade sources said exporters' demands had not been fully met. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
